summary.oneLiner: Sangam (India) Limited is a fully integrated textile company spanning fibre-to-fashion, and a leading manufacturer of PV dyed yarn and denim in India.
summary.business: Sangam (India) Limited operates across the entire textile value chain from fibre and yarn manufacturing to fabrics and garments, with a diversified portfolio spanning grey yarn, cotton blends, knitted fabrics, woven and processed fabrics, denim and garments. The Company serves government organisations, public and private companies, MSMEs, traders and proprietors domestically and exports to 52+ countries, with key partnerships including Walmart, Primark, Jockey, Decathlon and Mango.

currentContext.strengths: 'Integrated Shield': backward and forward integration across the value chain from fibre to fashion, reducing dependence on third-party fibre/yarn/fabric suppliers and maintaining supply continuity during global disruptions (e.g. Red Sea shipping crisis)|Circularity infrastructure recycling 38,400 MT of plastic waste into captive polyester fibre, meeting nearly 50% of daily polyester requirement and decoupling input costs from crude-oil volatility|Long-standing relationships with global retail brands (Walmart, Primark, Jockey, Decathlon, Mango) positioned as a 'Trusted Partner' rather than a mere supplier|Forward integration into branded seamless activewear (C9 Air Wear) with 2,000+ retail touchpoints and triple-digit digital D2C growth, supporting a shift from commodity yarn to branded apparel realisations|Scale: 3 Lakh+ spindles, ~65 MMPA weaving capacity, 10,000+ employees including 8,000+ skilled professionals, across 6 manufacturing facilities in Rajasthan
currentContext.strategies: 'Integrated Shield': strategic decision to own the value chain from fibre to fashion, providing production stability and reliability of export commitments during global supply-chain disruption|Input security through recycled polyester fibre (circularity) that decouples a significant portion of raw-material cost from volatile global crude-oil prices|Energy resilience: building a renewable (solar + wind/hybrid) energy portfolio as a structural hedge against rising industrial power tariffs|'Asset Sweating': maximising utilisation of newly commissioned spindle and weaving capacity to capture domestic demand, rather than pursuing fresh large capex|Shift towards value-added products: increasing the share of fabrics, seamless wear and branded apparel segments that carry structurally higher margins|Maintaining a balanced, diversified product and geography mix (multi-segment revenue, ~64% domestic / 36% export) to de-risk earnings against demand or pricing disruption|Leveraging FTA momentum (India-Australia ECTA operational, UK-India FTA progressing) and Four-Star Export House status for pricing advantage in export markets|Deepening high-value, sticky relationships with marquee global brands (Walmart, Primark, Jockey, Decathlon, Mango) to reduce customer-concentration risk|Forward integration into brand-led, higher-realisation seamless activewear/athleisure via the C9 Air Wear brand|Product diversification through wholly-owned subsidiary Sangam Ventures Limited, set up to build a seamless-garment manufacturing facility using advanced fibre blends (polyamide, spandex, polypropylene, natural fibres) and enter high-growth textile segments
currentContext.expansion: Following a multi-year, capital-intensive capacity-building cycle, Sangam's gross block expanded from ~`1,872 Crore to ~`2,095 Crore by 2025-26, with all new capacities now fully operational; going forward, maintenance/modernisation capex is tightly optimised and capital allocation has shifted to debt reduction. During FY26 the Company undertook three named expansion initiatives: (i) acquisition of a Recycled Polyester Staple Fiber (RPSF) manufacturing unit at Village Lambia Kalan, Bhilwara, to reduce dependence on virgin polyester; (ii) a proposed 38.16 MWp captive solar power project across Bhilwara units and a Solar Park in Jaisalmer, with tentative DCCO of 1 July 2026; and (iii) a PV Yarn expansion-cum-modernisation programme at Bhilwara and Chittorgarh (new machinery, technology and infrastructure upgrades), with tentative DCCO of 1 April 2028. Historically, the Company's growth was built through a series of calibrated expansions, including a `504 Crore capex programme (2023) for yarn and synthetic fabric expansion that also upgraded fabric weaving capacity from 48 MMPA to 65 MMPA, and acquisition of a green-fibre plant (16,020 MTPA / 45 TPD capacity) completed in 2025 alongside the spinning division's spindle/rotor/knitting-machine expansion.

choice for brands diversifying sourcing away from a single geography|India's textile and apparel sector seen moving from a USD 174 Billion base to a USD 350 Billion ambition by 2029-30, supported by risks.note: The industry remains exposed to global commodity cycles; fluctuations in domestic cotton yields and volatile crude oil prices continue to challenge pricing strategies and pressure margin stability.

Competition from Bangladesh, Vietnam and Cambodia remains intense, as these countries benefit from lower labour costs, efficient port logistics, and long-standing duty-free access to key Western markets.
Global supply chains remain fragile; regional conflicts, shipping disruptions, sudden policy shifts and geopolitical flare-ups can quickly disrupt logistics.

risks.risk: Stringent ESG compliance and non-tariff barriers
risks.note: Rapidly evolving ESG regulations, including carbon border taxes and traceability laws, are emerging as significant non-tariff barriers to exports.

risks.risk: Elevated leverage from the completed capex cycle
risks.note: Debt-to-equity ratio rose to 1.14x in FY2025-26 from 1.06x in FY2024-25, and interest coverage, while improved to 2.12x from 1.49x, remains modest, reflecting the higher finance costs from the recently concluded capacity expansion.
The current ratio declined to 1.11x (including current maturities of long-term debt) in FY2025-26 from 1.19x in FY2024-25.
Exports account for 35% to 40% of total revenue; while geographically diversified, this exposes the Company to region-specific macroeconomic and trade-policy risks.

one-line thesis: Sangam has completed its multi-year capex cycle, driving volume growth and margin expansion through higher capacity utilization and improved product mix; the one-time depreciation policy change boosted PAT, but underlying EBITDA margin growth of 120 bps to 9.6% is sustainable and supported by operational efficiencies and falling raw material costs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +16% YoY; EBITDA: +32% YoY, margin +120 bps to 9.6%; PAT (reported): +317% YoY (includes INR9cr one-time gain from depreciation change); PAT (normalized): ~INR14cr; Order book: Improving, especially in garments (utilization up from 25% to 35%); Net debt: Expected to decline by INR350cr over 3 years with no major capex planned
guidance: Revenue growth: 12-15% FY26; EBITDA margin: Targeting 11-12% in next 2 quarters; Order inflow: Stable export mix (35-40%); Capex/commissioning: No major capex planned; maintenance capex: INR50-70cr/year; 12MW captive solar to commission Dec 2025
order book & pipeline: Garment division order book has improved significantly; utilization up to 35% from 25% last quarter; expected to reach 60-65% next quarter; other divisions operating near full capacity
segment / subsidiary detail: Cotton yarn: 90%+ utilization; Denim/PV fabric: 85-90% utilization, 10-15% upside; Garments: 35% utilization, targeting 60-65% in Q3; EBITDA margins range 8-12% across segments; working capital cycle: 30-45 days longer for fabric vs yarn
growth verticals / optionality: Garment division capacity utilization to rise to 60-65% in next 2 quarters; potential for 10-12% further utilization gain in denim/fabric; export market stability (35-40% of revenue); no major capex planned, organic growth from utilization and mix
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin expansion driven by: 1) Bottomed-out cotton/yarn prices (Q1 to Q2: +2-3% yarn price increase, cycle stabilized); 2) Higher capacity utilization; 3) Newer, more efficient capex assets; 4) Product mix shift toward higher-margin items; 5) Upcoming INR10cr/year savings from 12MW captive solar (Dec 2025)
capex / expansion: Gross block increased from INR900cr to INR1,800cr over last 2 years; major capex cycle complete; no large capex planned for next 12-18 months; maintenance/modernization capex: INR50-70cr/year
capital allocation: Prioritizing debt reduction (INR100-120cr/year repayment); no dividend policy mentioned; focus on maximizing ROI from existing capex; no M&A or new verticals planned; ROCE target: 12% within 12-18 months
risks & watch-items: Cotton price volatility (30-35% import reliance temporarily); U.S. apparel tariffs (indirect exposure via customers); global demand slowdown; no pricing pressure from Bangladesh/China; no material inventory markdowns
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and operationally focused; emphasizes sustainability, efficiency, and capital discipline; dismisses near-term macro risks; avoids overpromising on margins or capex; transparent on one-offs
non-obvious takeaways: Despite INR23cr PAT, normalized PAT is ~INR14cr after depreciation one-off; 70% of power to be renewable in 15-18 months (from 15% today); garment division’s 35% utilization is a turnaround from 4 straight quarters of decline; export revenue not impacted by U.S. tariffs due to routing via Bangladesh/Africa
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U.S. apparel tariffs | Indian apparel exporters | loser | High | Sangam avoids direct exposure via fabric/yarn exports routed through Bangladesh/Africa, unlike pure-play garment exporters |

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.
